# Database schema reference

<!-- GENERATED by tests/ArcaneCore.World.Tests/Docs (SchemaReferenceRenderer) from DataModules and the context schema definitions. Do not edit by hand.
     Regenerate: ARCANECORE_UPDATE_DOCS=1 dotnet test tests/ArcaneCore.World.Tests --filter Docs -->

ArcaneCore keeps three logical databases (auth, characters, world), each with its own schema version in a `<component>_schema` table. A feature adds its tables by implementing `IDataModule` (the seam table is in docs/integration/seams.md); a component's versions run 2, 3, ... without gaps or duplicates and a gap fails at start before any database is touched. The version numbers are allocated by the integrator and renumbered at merge time, so the tables below show this tree's numbering only.

Upgrading an existing database is described in the [database upgrade runbook](../ops/database-upgrade.md); how each engine behaves while a step runs (MariaDB DDL commits implicitly, PostgreSQL DDL is transactional) is in the runbook and in [schema index repair](../integration/schema-index-repair.md). This page is metadata only: it reads the definitions and does not prove any behaviour of a database engine.

| Component | Current version | Version-1 base tables |
|---|---|---|
| `auth` | 5 | `account`, `realmlist` |
| `characters` | 42 | `characters` |
| `world` | 42 | `player_create_info`, `race_info`, `class_info` |

The last column is `yes` when the owning module implements or registers an `ICharacterDataCleanup` (it runs inside the character-deletion transaction); `no` means the module registers none; `-` is a step owned by the database context itself.
